name: sikhism
followers: about 25 to 30 million, most in the punjab
founder: guru nanak, followed by nine more human gurus
scriptures: the guru granth sahib, treated as the living guru
places: the harmandir sahib (golden temple) in amritsar, and the five takhts
summary: devotion to the one creator, remembered through god's name, honest work, and sharing with others. it teaches that all people are equal, and it was shaped by ten gurus over two centuries.
creation: before creation there was only the one, formless and in deep stillness. by god's will, the hukam, the universe came to be, with countless worlds and skies.
age: guru nanak taught that only the creator knows when the world was made: no scholar, holy book, or calendar can say. many sikhs see science and scripture as describing the same vast creation.

events.text: "for endless ages there was only darkness." there was no earth and no sky, no day or night, no sun or moon: only the one, in deep, formless stillness
by the hukam, the will of the one, the universe comes into being: "with one word you made the vast expanse, and hundreds of thousands of rivers began to flow"
guru nanak sings of worlds beneath worlds and hundreds of thousands of skies above, too many to count
"what was that time, what was that moment ... when the world was made?" no scholar or holy book knows; only the creator knows
nanak is born at talwandi, now nankana sahib in pakistan, into a hindu family
nanak goes into the river bein and disappears for three days. he returns saying "there is no hindu, there is no muslim", and begins his mission
guru nanak makes long journeys with the musician mardana, across india and, by tradition, to tibet, sri lanka, mecca, and baghdad
guru nanak settles at kartarpur, where his followers farm, pray, sing, and eat together
guru nanak dies, naming his disciple angad as the second guru; guru angad spreads the gurmukhi script
guru amar das insists that everyone, rich or poor, eat together in the langar before meeting him
guru ram das founds the city of amritsar around a sacred pool
guru arjan compiles the adi granth, the sikh scripture, and installs it in the harmandir sahib at amritsar
guru arjan is tortured and put to death on the orders of the mughal emperor jahangir, the first sikh martyr
guru hargobind wears two swords, for spiritual and worldly power, and builds the akal takht
guru tegh bahadur is beheaded in delhi on aurangzeb's orders after defending the right of hindus to keep their faith
at the vaisakhi festival, guru gobind singh founds the khalsa, the order of initiated sikhs, with the five beloved ones
before he dies, guru gobind singh declares that the scripture, the guru granth sahib, will be the guru forever
banda singh bahadur, who led a sikh uprising against mughal rule, is captured and executed in delhi
ranjit singh takes lahore and goes on to build the sikh empire
under ranjit singh the upper floors of the harmandir sahib are covered in gold, and it becomes known as the golden temple
after two wars, the british conquer the punjab
british troops fire on a crowd gathered in the jallianwala bagh at amritsar on vaisakhi day, killing hundreds
partition splits the punjab between india and pakistan; millions of sikhs leave their homes in the west
the indian army storms the golden temple; after indira gandhi is killed by her sikh bodyguards, thousands of sikhs are murdered in riots
about 25 to 30 million sikhs live mostly in the punjab, with large communities in britain, canada, and the united states
by remembering god's name and living truthfully, the soul is freed from ego and merges with the one, like a drop of water in the ocean

people.name: guru nanak
people.role: the first guru and founder of sikhism
people.about: taught devotion to the one god, honest work, sharing, and the equality of all people

people.name: bhai mardana
people.about: a muslim who played the rebab and traveled with guru nanak for decades, setting his hymns to music

people.name: guru angad
people.about: spread the gurmukhi script and wrestling and exercise for young sikhs

people.name: mata khivi
people.about: ran the langar, the free kitchen, and is the only woman named in the guru granth sahib

people.name: guru amar das
people.about: became guru at 73; spoke against caste, the veiling of women, and the burning of widows

people.name: guru ram das
people.about: founded amritsar and wrote the hymn sung at sikh weddings

people.name: guru arjan
people.about: compiled the adi granth, built the harmandir sahib with doors on all four sides, and was martyred

people.name: guru hargobind
people.about: taught that sikhs must be both saints and soldiers

people.name: guru har rai
people.about: known for his gentleness and for keeping herbal medicine gardens

people.name: guru har krishan
people.about: became guru at five and died at eight after caring for the sick during an epidemic in delhi

people.name: guru tegh bahadur
people.about: gave his life for the religious freedom of others

people.name: guru gobind singh
people.about: poet and warrior who founded the khalsa and made the scripture the eternal guru

people.name: mata sahib kaur
people.about: honored as the mother of the khalsa

people.name: banda singh bahadur
people.about: led a revolt against mughal rule and gave land to the peasants who worked it

people.name: ranjit singh
people.about: built a strong sikh empire, tolerant of all faiths, and covered the golden temple in gold

glossary.definition: "nectar": the sweetened water used when a sikh is initiated into the khalsa.
the five signs worn by initiated sikhs: kesh (uncut hair), kara (steel bracelet), kanga (comb), kachera (cotton undershorts), and kirpan (small sword).
"the guru's door": a sikh place of worship, where the guru granth sahib is kept and the langar is served.
"from the guru's mouth": the script in which the punjabi language and the guru granth sahib are written.
"teacher": in sikhism, the ten human gurus from nanak to gobind singh, and after them the scripture itself.
the sikh scripture, with hymns by six gurus and by hindu and muslim saints, treated as the living guru.
the will or order of god, by which everything happens.
"there is one god": the first words of the guru granth sahib, and the symbol of sikhism.
the community of initiated sikhs, founded by guru gobind singh in 1699.
singing the hymns of the scripture to music, the heart of sikh worship.
the free kitchen in every gurdwara, where all sit together and eat the same food, whatever their caste or faith.
worldly and spiritual power, shown by guru hargobind's two swords.
remembering god by repeating and meditating on god's name.
"the five beloved ones": the first five sikhs initiated into the khalsa in 1699.
the congregation of sikhs gathered in worship.
selfless service to others, without thought of reward.
the spring harvest festival, on which the khalsa was founded in 1699.
"wonderful lord": the name sikhs most often use for god.
